overview.headline: Wright brothers tested early lift formula to size wings

keyPoints.point: Designers needed enough aerodynamic lift to overcome aircraft weight
keyPoints.quote: They knew that they needed to generate enough aerodynamic lift to overcome the weight of their aircraft.

keyPoints.point: Lift grows with square of velocity and linearly with surface area
keyPoints.quote: lift depends on the square of the velocity and varies linearly with the surface area of the object.

keyPoints.point: Historic lift formula multiplies Smeaton coefficient velocity area and lift coefficient
keyPoints.quote: where L is the lift, k is the Smeaton coefficient, V is the velocity, A is the wing area, and cl is the lift coefficient.

keyPoints.point: Brothers began to doubt Smeaton coefficient value and determined value more closely approximated data
keyPoints.quote: the brothers began to doubt the .005 value for the Smeaton coefficient and they determined that a value of .0033 more closely approximated their data.

keyTerms.gloss: upward aerodynamic force that must overcome weight to fly
keyTerms.quote: They knew that they needed to generate enough aerodynamic lift to overcome the weight of their aircraft.

keyTerms.gloss: coefficient representing pressure force on moving flat plate
portion of pressure force converted into lift for a shape
keyTerms.quote: they represented that portion by a lift coefficient.

keyTerms.gloss: angle of body inclination to flow
keyTerms.quote: also called the angle of attack.

keyTerms.gloss: surface area over which air flows to generate lift
